title: Fix suggest_profit_target to use the weekly chart's channel, not the daily
description: Ch. 39 p.161 ('Stops and Profit Targets' section), read directly: 'Triple Screen calls for setting profit targets using long-term charts and stops on the charts of your intermediate timeframe... When buying a dip on a daily chart, the value zone on a weekly chart presents a good target.' This app's intermediate timeframe is daily (Wave/Screen 2) and long-term is weekly (Tide/Screen 1) -- but suggest_profit_target's channel/support-resistance target and protective_stop's SafeZone stop are both currently computed entirely off daily data. Per this explicit rule, the profit target should be drawn from the weekly chart's channel/value-zone instead; the stop staying on daily is already correct and does not change.

checklist.step: Change suggest_profit_target's channel computation to use weekly OHLCV instead of daily, per ch.39 p.161's explicit stops-vs-targets timeframe rule.
Confirm protective_stop remains on daily data (already correct per the same rule) -- no change needed there, but verify explicitly rather than assuming.
Update the existing hand-computed reference-value tests for suggest_profit_target with new expected values reflecting the weekly-based target.
Record a decisions entry noting this corrects a prior implementation now that the primary source (ch. 39 p.161) has been read directly rather than inferred.
Regenerate backend/openapi.json/frontend types if the response shape changes (should not -- this only changes which data feeds an existing field).

decisions.decision: suggest_profit_target's signature changed from taking already-computed `channel_upper`/`channel_lower: float | None` (previously sourced by the caller from app.signals.engine.analyse's DAILY Autoenvelope pass) to taking a `weekly_ohlcv: pd.DataFrame` parameter and computing the weekly Autoenvelope channel internally via a new private `_weekly_channel_bounds` helper (autoenvelope(weekly_ohlcv['close'], ema_period=13), default deviation_lookback=100 -- i.e. a ~100-WEEK warm-up, not 100-day). The support/resistance ('Position-style') candidate and the caller's already-detected `zones` stay daily and unchanged -- ch. 39 p.161's quoted rule is specifically about the channel/value-zone target ('the value zone on a weekly chart'), not the support/resistance technique, and app.signals.support_resistance has no weekly variant. protective_stop/stop_from_price_action (app.portfolio.risk) was verified unchanged and still daily-only, per the same rule (it is Triple Screen's intermediate-timeframe half of the stops-vs-targets split, already correct before this fix).
decisions.rationale: Considered and rejected: (1) keeping the channel_upper/channel_lower float parameters and just having the caller (get_analysis in stocks.py) source them from a NEW weekly autoenvelope pass computed in the router instead -- rejected because the channel computation itself is what the checklist calls out as needing to move ('Change suggest_profit_target's channel computation'), and because this weekly channel has no other consumer to share a precompute-and-share pattern with (unlike `zones`, which IS shared with AnalysisResponse.support_resistance_zones) -- computing it fresh inside profit_target.py from a raw weekly_ohlcv input keeps the caller simpler (one fewer explicit computation in the router) and keeps the 'what feeds this candidate' logic colocated with the rest of the target-selection code. (2) Exposing ema_period/deviation_lookback as overridable kwargs on suggest_profit_target purely to make unit tests easier to hand-verify with a small window -- rejected as unnecessary production-signature bloat for a test-only need; the unit tests instead build a realistic-length (120-row) weekly fixture and cross-check the expected channel bounds via a direct call to the already-independently-hand-verified `autoenvelope()` function (see tests/unit/indicators/test_autoenvelope.py), the same 'reuse an already-verified building block as the reference value' pattern this test file already used for its protective-stop fixture (cross-referenced from test_portfolio_risk.py) before this change. (3) Deriving deviation_lookback specifically for weekly use (e.g. a shorter number since 100 weeks is ~2 years) -- rejected since nothing in docs/Analyse.md or Elder's own text calls for a different lookback just because the bar interval changed from daily to weekly, and introducing an unexplained second number would be exactly the kind of undocumented judgment call this app's decision-memory convention exists to avoid; kept autoenvelope's own existing default unchanged.

decisions.decision: Addressing pr-decision's needs_work override: updated the three stale frontend copy locations it named (frontend/src/utils/profitTargetHelpText.ts's shared PROFIT_TARGET_DEFINITION, and the identical sourceLabel/no-candidate phrases duplicated in both features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts and features/portfolio/components/metricHelpContent.ts) to describe the weekly-chart-based channel ('the weekly chart's Autoenvelope/channel height', '~100 weeks of weekly history') instead of the pre-fix daily wording. Also found and fixed the same stale-copy regression in two places pr-decision's finding didn't enumerate but that are the same class of bug: backend/app/api/schemas.py's ProfitTargetOut.source and AnalysisResponse.profit_target field descriptions (the OpenAPI contract frontend/src/api/types.ts is generated from) still said 'today's Autoenvelope/channel height' and '~100 days of history', and source's description additionally claimed the channel was 'the same channel AnalysisResponse.indicators.channel_upper/channel_lower expose' -- which became actively false once the channel moved to weekly while indicators.channel_upper/lower stayed daily. Regenerated backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts from the corrected schemas (docs/Analyse.md itself was already correct from the original commit -- only schemas.py and the three named frontend files had drifted). Added regression tests per the review comment's own suggestion: frontend/src/utils/profitTargetHelpText.test.ts (new file, asserts PROFIT_TARGET_DEFINITION mentions the weekly chart and not 'today's'), plus new cases in both features/stocks and features/portfolio metricHelpContent.test.ts asserting profitTargetHelp.interpretValue's channel sourceLabel and no-candidate text mention 'weekly'/'weeks' and not 'today's'/'days'.
decisions.rationale: Fixing only the three explicitly named locations and leaving schemas.py stale was rejected: CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard requires every Pydantic field description to stay accurate, frontend/src/api/types.ts is generated FROM openapi.json (so leaving schemas.py stale would have left a fourth, larger surface silently describing the old daily behavior even after the three named frontend files were fixed), and the 'same channel indicators exposes' claim in source's description was not just outdated wording but a now-incorrect factual claim about which computation feeds the field. Chose word-for-word-parallel test assertions in both stocks/portfolio metricHelpContent.test.ts files (rather than extracting a single shared test helper) to match the existing convention in this codebase of two independent, near-identical test files mirroring the two near-identical production registries (see this task's first decisions entry and both metricHelpContent.ts files' own top-of-file comments on why a cross-feature import isn't used) -- a shared test helper would cut against that same established convention for a marginal DRY gain.

decisions.decision: Addressed pr-reviewer's fresh needs_work finding: rewrote docs/architecture/API.md's `profit_target` paragraph (line 169) to say the channel candidate is computed from the *weekly* chart's Autoenvelope/channel height (ch. 39 p.161's stops-on-intermediate/targets-on-long-term rule) and is a separate computation from the *daily* `indicators.channel_upper`/`channel_lower`, and changed 'under ~100 days of history' to 'under ~100 weeks of weekly history' -- matching the wording already fixed in schemas.py and the three frontend copy locations. Given this exact bug class had recurred 5 times across this PR's review rounds, also did the thorough grep sweep the review comment requested (docs/, backend/, frontend/, for 'today's Autoenvelope', 'channel_upper'/'channel_lower', '~100 days'/'100-bar' near any profit_target/suggest_profit_target mention) before treating this as the last instance. Found one more, previously uncaught: frontend/src/features/methodology/data/methodologyContent.ts's `profit-target` entry summary still read 'that day's Autoenvelope/channel height' -- fixed to 'the weekly chart's Autoenvelope/channel height' with the ch. 39 p.161 citation added, matching profitTargetHelpText.ts's wording. Every other channel_upper/channel_lower/~100-bar mention found by the sweep (docs/Analyse.md's grading section, backend/app/portfolio/grading.py, the trade-grading OpenAPI descriptions, PriceChart.tsx, engine.py, the indicator-history endpoint docs) is about the DAILY channel indicator itself (trade-grading capture %, the price-chart overlay, /indicators history) -- a genuinely separate computation from profit_target's channel candidate, correctly left as-is. Historical `docs/tasks/done/backend-profit-target.json`'s own description/decisions text (pre-dating this fix) was also left untouched -- it's an immutable record of what was true when that task was done, the same as prior git history, not a currently-read living doc.
decisions.rationale: Fixing only the one location pr-reviewer named, without re-running the sweep, was rejected given the review's own explicit ask and the track record (5 recurrences across 2 rounds already) -- a 6th miss would very likely trigger yet another needs_work round. Leaving docs/tasks/done/backend-profit-target.json's historical text untouched was considered and rejected as a candidate fix, then re-rejected: that file is a snapshot of a decision made before this task existed, analogous to a closed PR's diff -- 'living' documentation that readers currently consult for the truth (API.md, schemas.py, the frontend help copy, methodologyContent.ts) is what this bug class is actually about; rewriting a past task's own historical decision record to match a later correction would erase, not preserve, the record of what was decided when.

comments.summary: docs/architecture/API.md's `profit_target` paragraph (the `source: "channel"` sentence) still says 'current close + 30% of today's Autoenvelope/channel height, the same channel `indicators.channel_upper`/`channel_lower` expose' and 'under ~100 days of history' -- the exact same stale-copy bug class pr-decision's prior override caught in three frontend files and task-worker's fix additionally caught in backend/app/api/schemas.py, but missed here. Both claims are now factually wrong post-fix: the channel is the WEEKLY chart's (a separate computation from the daily indicators.channel_upper/channel_lower), and the warm-up is ~100 WEEKS. This file predates this PR (untouched by any commit here) but is CLAUDE.md's own designated source-of-truth doc for the API -- leaving it stale risks misleading a future reader/tool the same way the frontend copy did. BLOCKING: same bug class as the prior needs_work round, in a location neither pass covered.
